subject: geography
title: Scale, Symbols and Contours
welcome_lead: Maps show huge areas on small paper. Discover scale, symbols and the magical lines that reveal hills — contours!
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on map scale, symbols and contour lines.
final_note: Excellent! You can now read maps in full detail.

walkthroughs.body_html: A scale of 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map = 50,000 cm (500 m) in real life. Big number = less detail, more area shown.
Symbols stand for real features: a blue line is a river, a green triangle a campsite, P for parking. Always check the key.
Contour lines join places at the same height. Close together = steep; far apart = gentle. Each line usually shows 10m intervals on OS maps.

mcqs.q: Why are there no volcanoes at conservative plate boundaries?
options: There are volcanoes at conservative boundaries — that's where most of them form.
There are no volcanoes because the boundaries are too cold.
Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.
Conservative boundaries involve plates sliding past each other horizontally — no crust is created or destroyed, so there is no subduction to generate magma.

mcqs.q: What are the three cells of global atmospheric circulation?
options: The Hadley cell (equator to 30 degrees), Ferrel cell (30 to 60 degrees) and Polar cell (60 degrees to poles) together redistribute heat from equator to poles.
There is one big Hadley cell from the equator to each pole.
There are volcanoes at conservative boundaries — that's where most of them form.
The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.

mcqs.q: What is the 'race to the bottom' critique of globalisation?
options: The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.

The argument that TNCs play countries off against each other, relocating to those with lowest wages, weakest regulation and lowest taxes — pressuring governments to cut standards to attract investment.
The race to the bottom means TNCs compete with each other for the lowest prices.
Race to the bottom is when companies offshore work to mines and underground factories.
